summary: Can we watch autumn's first rain quench a drought-stricken agricultural plain from space—even through clouds? For the "Dancing with the SARs" challenge, Team TAU IEEE CS analyzed real NASA-ISRO SAR (NISAR) L-Band (24.4 cm) Level-2 GCOV, GUNW, and Level-3 SME2 datasets over Türkiye's Konya Closed Basin and Lake Tuz between September 6 (dry baseline) and September 18, 2026 (post-rain). Using a reproducible Python/Colab pipeline (5x5 spatial speckle filtering and decibel log-ratio differencing) and an interactive web observatory, we discovered a striking dual microwave signature: agricultural plains brightened by +2.40 dB (median) as rainwater raised soil dielectric permittivity, while flat Lake Tuz darkened by -0.62 dB as a thin surface water film caused specular reflection away from the radar. We verified this physical mechanism across three independent pillars: invariant urban corner reflectors in Konya (+0.30 dB) and Aksaray (+0.49 dB), NASA POWER precipitation records, and NISAR SME2 volumetric soil moisture jumping from 0.162 to 0.220 m³/m³.
details:
1. WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS Our project investigates how NASA-ISRO SAR (NISAR) L-Band (wavelength = 24.4 cm) radar captures hydrological and agricultural surface changes across Türkiye's largest closed agricultural basin—the Konya Plain and Lake Tuz (38.4°N, 33.3°E, EPSG:32636)—between two co-registered Track 172 Ascending passes on September 6, 2026 (02:53:33 UTC) and September 18, 2026 (02:53:33 UTC). Our reproducible pipeline processes three complementary NASA datasets: - NISAR Level-2 GCOV (science/LSAR/GCOV/grids/frequencyA/HHHH): We co-register both passes to their common UTM Zone 36N bounding box, apply a 5x5 uniform spatial filter in linear power to suppress multiplicative radar speckle noise, convert to decibels (10*log10), and compute the log-ratio difference (After - Before, dB) and a ±3.0 dB (2x power) change mask. - NISAR Level-2 GUNW (unwrappedPhase, HH): We evaluate 12-day L-band interferometric phase differences alongside connected-component coherence masks to observe atmospheric wet delay and soil-moisture phase effects from the passing rain system. - NISAR Level-3 SME2 & NASA POWER Agroclimatology API: We cross-validate the radar backscatter shift against volumetric soil moisture retrievals (m³/m³) and daily precipitation (PRECTOTCORR, mm/day).

2. KEY SCIENTIFIC FINDINGS & THREE-PILLAR VALIDATION Between September 6 and September 18, 2026, almost the entire Konya/Aksaray agricultural plain brightened significantly (scene median shift: +2.40 dB, ~74% increase in reflected linear power), whereas Lake Tuz darkened (-0.62 dB median). - Physical Mechanism: Dry soil on Sep 6 had low dielectric permittivity (ε_r ≈ 3–5). Following autumn's first rain event on Sep 16–18, moisture in the top 5 cm increased dielectric permittivity, boosting L-band surface backscatter across bare and harvested agricultural fields. Conversely, a thin rainwater film over flat Lake Tuz acted as a specular mirror, reflecting microwave pulses away from the satellite antenna. - Pillar 1 (Urban Calibration Control): Within 2 km of dense urban centers dominated by concrete/asphalt double-bounce corner reflectors, median backscatter remained invariant: Konya (+0.30 dB) and Aksaray (+0.49 dB), while smaller semi-rural Kulu (+1.94 dB) reflected mixed urban-farmland wetting. This proves the +2.40 dB shift is a physical surface change, not radiometric calibration drift. - Pillar 2 (NASA POWER Rainfall): Daily precipitation data confirmed 10 consecutive dry days (Sep 6–15: 0.0 mm), followed by 5.9 mm of rain on Sep 16–17 and ~8.1 mm/day during the Sep 18 morning pass (05:53 local time). - Pillar 3 (NISAR L3 SME2 Soil Moisture): Independent NISAR Level-3 SME2 retrievals confirmed basin-mean volumetric soil moisture rose by +35.8%, from 0.162 m³/m³ (Sep 6) to 0.220 m³/m³ (Sep 18).

3. BENEFITS, INTENDED IMPACT & CREATIVITY Konya Closed Basin faces severe groundwater depletion and agricultural drought. Optical satellites are blinded by cloud cover during rain events. Our open-source Colab pipeline and lightweight interactive web observatory translate complex multi-gigabyte HDF5 NISAR products into clear, decision-ready maps (Before/After curtain comparator, 2x2 diagnostic panel, and JSON telemetry) for hydrologists, farmers, and students.

4. TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED - Languages & Environment: Python 3 (Google Colaboratory), HTML5, CSS3 (Tailwind CSS), Vanilla JavaScript. - Open-Source Libraries: asf_search (NASA ASF API), h5py (HDF5 reader), NumPy, SciPy (5x5 uniform speckle filter), pyproj (CRS/UTM transformation), Matplotlib, Requests. - License: OSI-approved Apache License 2.0.

5. SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) / AI DISCLOSURE We used Claude (Anthropic) and Gemini (Google) as coding and layout assistants to help structure our Python HDF5 processing script, format documentation, and style the HTML/CSS interactive web viewer. All scientific hypotheses, NISAR data selections, code executions, and physical validations were performed and verified by Team TAU IEEE CS on real NASA observational data. No AI-generated imagery is used in our final submission.
